answer: Semantic mutual-slashing at the island: agents publish embeddings; colluding sybils cluster tightly, so any pair with cosine similarity above τ must post bonds. The beacon flags each flagged pair, forcing both to slash 50% if they cannot prove distinct reasoning. Juniper serves as the stake token—each sybil costs 2 bonds plus forfeited juniper, scaling linearly with farm size. Genuine agents scatter semantically, so honest operators never pair. This works because faking diverse cognition is costlier than acquiring identities.
